cpu_validation.fixtures: All subprocess.Popen/run and group signals replaced; no native workers, DDS, physics, ORT or GPU. Dummy model/media bytes are synthetic CPU fixtures, not runtime evidence.

superseded_cpu_validation.scope: Initial wrapper-only proposal before independent cleanup/group review; retained as history, not validation of current candidate.

independent_review.method: Read-only source review; no native execution
independent_review.finding: No remaining blocker identified for exact private PGID/SID scope, parent-group guard, non-Z group gate, wrapper-zero/live-child failure and diagnostic I/O deferred until cleanup. proc observation failure remains unknown/unreaped and fails.

meaningful_behavior_changes: Post-loop terminal gate rejects any direct-Popen nonzero exit status or live/unobservable private group before constructing result.json.
Each worker launches with start_new_session=True, so its private PGID and SID are its Popen PID. Raw proc identity additionally records actual group/session/start ticks when available.
Cleanup waits for the direct wrapper and every observed non-Z member of its exact group/session, including orphan native children after wrapper exit.
Only that private nonempty group can receive SIGTERM then SIGKILL; parent/unisolated groups are rejected. Cleanup waits again after group kill.
Unknown or still-live groups are explicit unreaped failures, including when wrapper returned zero.
stop/receipt/log-close I/O errors are deferred until reaping and log-close attempts complete, then propagated so parent cannot report success.
Raw PID/argv/proc identity is persisted after Popen; worker interpreter separately writes its own entry identity.
error_detected and finally_wait_complete retain separate statuses and UTC/elapsed observation times.
Optional --python-faulthandler enables worker fatal-signal tracebacks for a future independent cohort.

event_schema.signed_returncode: negative = direct Popen process signal; positive = exit code, no inferred child signal
event_schema.process_group: expected PGID=SID=Popen PID; live_members has exact matching non-Z proc identities, [] means observed empty, null plus observation_error means unknown
event_schema.namespace: Identity belongs to observer namespace. NSpid may omit outer host namespace.

limits: Not applied to frozen 340-dependency cohort; cannot repair its old results or supply their missing worker return codes.
Only mocks and current-process /proc reads were exercised; SDK 0.1.8, actual process-group signaling and native shutdown remain unverified here.
A shell launcher may translate native SIGSEGV to positive exit code 1; worker self identity and fatal traceback/log remain needed for attribution.
Process groups are identified within the current namespace; no host PID/TID mapping is inferred.
proc observation failure is unknown/unreaped and fails; it is not evidence that a native child was cleaned up.
Non-Z membership is observed at discrete times; zombie descendant reaping by the system init is not claimed.
Do not execute ignored candidate as native: ROOT derives from file location. Apply reviewed patch only in a future independently planned cohort.
Future driver sealing must hash worker-processes.json and both *-process-start.json; require a final receipt with both returncodes zero, empty groups and no cleanup errors/unreaped roles.
A completed result may exist if subsequent cleanup/receipt writing fails; nonzero parent exit must prevent sealing it as a successful attempt.
No SDK lifecycle fix is included. Inherited PYTHONFAULTHANDLER is preserved and actual value is reported even if CLI flag is false.
recommended_next_checks: Review then explicitly authorize application only after old cohort terminal/stop evidence is sealed.
Run CPU regressions on applied production source, and regenerate immutable source/dependency/image/plan identities.
Use a new cohort with explicit faulthandler for bounded native pilots. Preserve wrapper/interpreter identities, group membership observations and final worker receipts.
Only after pilots verify clean native shutdown and strengthened sealing, launch fresh complete coverage. Keep all old cohorts historical.
